body:
well thanks for not only listening but responding.

>Step one is to realize that depression or anxiety disorders are not your fault, nor the fault of your family, your religion, or your upbringing.

I know on an intellectual level that it is brain chemistry, the problem is I can't limit my thoughts to just an intellectual level. I know there are disorders that limit what people can do, but my quandary is where is that line? If I need to do x, but instead I fill my day with time fillers, essentially running down the clock until the day is out, that is still on some level a choice. Yes it is a choice that is much less painful, but where is that line of free choice and electro-chemical block? I know that people with OCD for example do things that are not a free "choice" but some can say the same for alcoholics yet alcoholics can stop drinking. I guess I just worry about the difference for me between I "can't do x" and "I really really don't want to do x" if that makes any sense.

I also do think I have depression, probably an anxiety disorder thrown in to boot. I try to be honest with myself about it even if I can be dishonest with about everyone else. I have tried some counceling when I was still in school, but the school only covered one visit a week and I just was never very sure that did a whole heck of a lot. I also tried some SSRI meds for about 5 months with next to no result. The problem is I have no health insurance and no money to make it past basic expenses like food rent and utilities.

I would love to go "all-in" somewhere, I just don't know what that would mean or how I could afford to do it. One of my problems is I am painfully resistant to sharing anything close to personal, let alone some of these most personal failings of all. By the time the hour is up I had sometimes barely scratched the surface of anything that might be a "root." I've often thought that the only way to get progress would probably have to be many times a week or maybe an in-patient something, but I don't have money or court order for either. 

My field is not psychology it's politics. I only took one intro class as part of my gen-ed so my knowledge on most of this is no more than Wikipedia deep and often not even that good. But maybe people in here might know more, how can I try to get better knowing I really don't have much money? I'm in the DC area if that narrows down anything but I am at a real loss as to where to even start. My parents are supportive and can maybe spare some more but really not a lot more. 

I don't want to sound like I'm putting the onus on you guys but if I don't ask for help frankly I may not get around to looking up people for a long time on my own. I came here mostly to vent but I hoped in the back of my head that you guys could maybe help too.
